title: How analytics events are used in practice
description: Practical uses for analytics events — funnels, retention, revenue, debugging — and which tool categories support each job.
quickAnswer: Teams use events to measure **funnels** (step completion), **retention** (return behavior), **revenue** (purchases tied to journeys), and **debugging** (what failed before support tickets). Pageview-only tools cover light goals; product analytics tools cover the rest.

sections.title: Funnels
sections.content:
A funnel is an ordered set of events: `signup_started` → `email_verified` → `project_created`. You care about drop-off between steps, not just landing-page traffic.

**Best fit:** PostHog, mature GA4 explorations. **Light goals only:** Plausible/Fathom custom events — useful for one conversion, weak for multi-step product funnels.

sections.title: Retention and engagement
sections.content:
Retention asks whether users come back and do the core action again. That requires **stable identity** and a clear "active" event.

Product analytics tools are built for this. Web analytics tools usually stop at returning visitors by cookie or cookieless approximation — a different question.

sections.title: Revenue and attribution
sections.content:
Two common patterns:

- **Ecommerce / purchase events** inside GA4 or PostHog
- **Payment-provider attribution** (e.g. DataFast + Stripe) that ties revenue to the visit that led to checkout

Pick the pattern that matches how you sell. Indie SaaS often wants channel → paid customer; marketplaces want item-level purchase events.

sections.title: Debugging UX with events (and replay)
sections.content:
Events tell you *that* something failed (`checkout_error`). Session replay and heatmaps help you see *why*. Hotjar and PostHog sit in that adjacent lane — heavier privacy and performance review required.

Instrument the failure event first; add replay only where tickets prove you need video.

sections.title: Keep the event list small
sections.content:
Every event has a cost: engineering time, quota, and dashboard trust. Prefer a short list of decision-grade events over autocapture of every click.

New to the idea of events? Start with [Analytics Events: What They Are and Why They Matter](/learn/what-are-analytics-events/).
